size.note: Newman's Birds gives 23 cm for the female and 41 cm for the male.

habitat: Among large trees along rivers, at forest fringes, on well-wooded hills and in suburbia.
summary: A common summer resident, present all year in the east and northeast. The crested head is deep blue-grey and grades to a grey breast. The bill and eye-ring are blue. The identification line says the upperparts and tail are chestnut-brown, and the description says the upperparts are orange-brown. The male has ribbon-like central tail feathers. The call is a sharp zwee-zwer, and the song is a lively trill. The Kemp name Paradise Flycatcher and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Blue-mantled Crested Flycatcher is dark brown above, with a white wing-bar and a black crest. Its call is almost the same.

upperparts.pattern: The identification line says chestnut-brown upperparts and tail. The description says orange-brown upperparts.
The identification line says chestnut-brown upperparts and tail. The description says orange-brown upperparts.

calls.description: A sharp 'zwee-zwer', almost the same as Blue-mantled Crested Flycatcher. The song is a lively 'wee-te-tiddly, wit-wit'. The grade A call is from Skukuza. The filename is XC1080072-Paradise-flycatcher-call-Kruger-Skukuza-260125-174812_Tr1-.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer resident and says it is present all year in the east and northeast. Kruger is in that region, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so the status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Chestnut-brown and orange-brown are both used for the upperparts, so no upperpart colour is stored. The grade A call is from Skukuza. The Kemp name Paradise Flycatcher and the code VB were left unchanged.
